BiblicalUsage: Harosheth of the Gentiles was the home of Sisera, captain of Jabin's host, with nine hundred chariots of iron. The LORD sold Israel into Jabin's hand, Sisera gathered his chariots from Harosheth to the river Kishon, and Barak pursued them back to Harosheth until not a man was left.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Harosheth is the measure of the victory: nine hundred iron chariots gathered there, and none came back. The place that launched the oppression became the place the pursuit ended.
